item.description:

Three amazing performers: Wondrous Jazz Veteran Linda Mitchell, Father of the MGB’s and Owner of Asheville Guitar Bar Mark Goldthwaite and Ovadya’s Amazing Singer Songwriter Poet Em Hurley. item.title: The Connect: Community Jam — Tue Oct 20, 8:00 PM — The One Stop
item.description:
Introducing The Connect: a weekly community jam at The One Stop curated by Women to the Front on Tuesdays, 8-11pm.
Asheville Music Hall The One Stop has a long history of being a place where musicians come together. The Connect is about continuing that spirit while helping create something new. This weekly jam aims to be a welcoming, respectful space where professional musicians, rising artists, and everyone in between can come together to collaborate, connect, and learn from each other.
Each week will feature a thoughtfully curated group of musicians who will start the night with a short set and then open the night to a jam. The goal is to build community across different generations, backgrounds, genres, and levels of experience. We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can feel safe, respected, and encouraged to attend.
Come play, come listen, come make some new friends, and help us reconnect with Asheville’s music community.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Oct 21 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.description: Hendo Fun Friends I am going to Cedar Rock Mtn in DuPont Forest; Up to 12 ppl are welcome to join. Cedar Rock Mountain in DuPont State Forest provides wonderful views and dramatic scenery - Cedar Rock Mountain contains some of the most exposed granite anywhere in the region. Hundreds of acres alternate between bare and moss/lichen covered rock. The area has become quite popular with mountain bikers and hikers. We will walk the Big Rock/ Cedar Rock/Little River/Corn Mill Shoals Tr(s). Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have pleasant surprises. **I will be carrying the ‘Ent-Ward’ that gives us permission to pass thru the forest.** Difficulty: eroded water outwash on uphill trail. Some rocks & roots. We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !! **https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4** Details: (Social ‘hour’ at 9:45 AM. item.title: Quinn Sternberg's Mind Beach — Mon Nov 2, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Dive into the sonic waves of Quinn Sternberg's Mind Beach—where jazz becomes a landscape and every note washes over you like tide meeting shore.
This isn't your typical Monday night. It's an expedition into the spaces between beats, where four master musicians construct entire worlds from reed, string, skin, and ivory. Quinn Sternberg's bass serves as your anchor, holding gravity steady while Jacob Rodriguez's baritone sax paints horizons in deep indigo. Joe Enright's drums pulse like the heartbeat beneath sand, and Alex Taub's piano keys shimmer like moonlight on water.
Mind Beach isn't a place—it's a state of being. It's where mountain soul meets metropolitan sophistication, where tradition and exploration shake hands and decide to dance. These aren't just players; they're archi...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall — Tue Nov 3, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...
Source: Little Jumbo

Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Please join me and other local writers for a group writing session. Bring whatever you're working on and grab a coffee, and we will write alongside each other.
This is not a critique group, but we do have short social periods before and after writing. \-\-\- Many have mentioned that The Dripolator is a little hard to find if you've never been before. The coffeeshop is located in a strip mall where the Candler YMCA is, and the sonic. The Dripolator is next to the bank, and looks a little like a house. There is usually plenty of parking in the lot out front. If you're having trouble send me a message!
